datasets.name: 10uk_summer_2026
datasets.summary_html:
LCDM chains of sample_joint on simulated lensed temperature maps: the summer 2026 run at 10 uK-arcmin, on Hugging Face as omch2_logA_theta_MC_100_joint_inference_09_02_26_high_noise.

Setting Value
Data Temperature only (I)
Map size 128 x 128 pixels at 2.5 arcmin per pixel
White noise level 10 uK-arcmin
Sampled parameters theta_MC_100, logA, omch2
Maps 10
Chains per map 5
Sweeps per chain 6000
Burn-in removed 600 sweeps per chain
Product distribution Gaussian: the product of one normal per map (its mean and std)
Product errors Bootstrap over each map's thinned samples (Monte Carlo error of the chains)
Fisher forecast Field blocks from the measured delensed covariance (Wiener filter from the QE N0 with unlensed filter and unlensed response); phi noise the QE N0 with unlensed filter and unlensed response
Parameter Ground truth Mean R-hat over maps Std of R-hat over maps Acceptance rate
theta_MC_100 1.031732 1.0067 0.0026 0.49
logA 3.218387 1.0043 0.0016 0.46
omch2 0.109381 1.0073 0.0048 0.49

Held at the ground truth: ns = 0.959814, ombh2 = 0.022386.

Notes written when the chains were run

  • 128 x 128 sized temperature only maps
  • theta_pix = 2.5
  • (f, phi) both sampled, phi using HMC with step_size = 0.05, num_steps = 10
  • working in mixed parametrization withOUT perfect G using cphi_fid
  • phi_init = ZEROES (MAP seems to sometimes go NaN for certain LCDM parameter combos)
  • 3 sequential 1-D MH steps for omch2, logA, theta_MC_100 with theta_MC_100_step = 4e-3, logA_step = 3.5e-2, omch2_step = 3.5e-3
  • Starting out at random initial points in the 3-D param space... (raised lower bound on omch2 from ~ 0.079 to 0.085)
  • No 1/f noise OR beam, only white noise at a noise-level of 10 uk-arcmin.
  • No mask
  • Using CAMB multi-dimensional interpolator instead of the emulator
  • map_prefix = 234567
  • num_burn_in_fix_theta = 100
  • 6000 iterations per sub-chain, 5 sub-chains per map, 10 maps
  • deterministic order of theta parameter sampling

datasets.name: 10uk
datasets.summary_html:
Lensing reconstruction noise of map_joint and of the Gibbs sampler (cosmological parameters held at the ground truth), compared with the quadratic-estimate noise N(0), at 10 uK-arcmin.

Setting Value
Data Temperature only (I)
Map size 128 x 128 pixels at 2.5 arcmin per pixel
White noise level 10 uK-arcmin, no 1/f noise, no beam
Joint MAP 100 realizations
Gibbs sampler 100 realizations, one chain per map, burn-in 600 sweeps
Curves Medians over bands of the multipole L; the shaded bands are a delete-one-realization jackknife
Source files map_joint_phi_noise_data/map_joint_phi_noise_output_10uk/map_joint_phi_noise.npz and sampler_phi_noise_data/sampler_phi_noise_output_10uk_pre_refactor/sampler_phi_noise_response.npz on Hugging Face

How the noise is measured

Each reconstruction is compared with the true lensing potential φtrue of its simulation, one Fourier mode at a time:

Nφ = Cφ (1 / r2 − 1)

Here Cφ is the power spectrum of the true lensing potential, and r2 is the fraction of the true potential that the reconstruction recovers: r2 = 1 gives no noise, and r2 near 0 gives a noise far above the signal. The angle brackets below are averages over the realizations, taken before the ratio is formed.

  • Joint MAP. r2 is the squared correlation of the MAP estimate φMAP with the true potential:

    r2 = ⟨Re(φMAP φtrue∗)⟩2 / ( ⟨|φMAP|2⟩ ⟨|φtrue|2⟩ )

  • Gibbs sampler. r2 is the response of the posterior mean φmean (the average of a chain's samples) to the true potential:

    r2 = ⟨Re(φmean φtrue∗)⟩ / ⟨|φtrue|2⟩

    The response is used here instead of the correlation because a chain is finite: its mean is the exact posterior mean plus a Monte Carlo error ε, φmean = φexact + ε. The correlation divides by ⟨|φmean|2⟩ = ⟨|φexact|2⟩ + ⟨|ε|2⟩, and the ⟨|ε|2⟩ term is never zero. It adds spurious power to the sampler mean, which lowers r2 and inflates the noise. The response never uses |φmean|2, and ε is not correlated with the true potential, so it averages out of ⟨Re(φmean φtrue∗)⟩. For the exact posterior mean the two definitions of r2 agree.

Notes

  • The sampler run has one chain per map, so its convergence cannot be checked with the Gelman-Rubin statistic. A chain that has not converged shows up as extra noise.
  • The sampler's posterior mean was not projected onto its Hermitian part in this run. Only the modes with kx = 0 and kx at the Nyquist frequency are affected.
